newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks close down on blue-chip selling.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks close down on blue-chip selling.

text.p: Thai stocks closed down on Tuesday after four consecutive trading days of rises as local retail investors sold blue-chip stocks and took profits from the run mild run up, brokers said.
The SET index fell 8.52 points to 1,050.35 on 4.2 billion baht turnover. Decliners led gainers 263 to 96 while 78 issues were unchanged. The SET-50 index slipped 0.63 point to 80.61.
"Local retail investors did the most selling and took profits today as they awaited a no-confidence motion debate against the prime minister tomorrow," said Samart Rusmeerojwong of James Capel Asia.
The finance sector fell heavily by 2.26 percent, followed by the property sector which dropped 1.39 percent and the energy sector retreated 1.07 percent.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list, falling two baht to 170. Finance One dropped three to 100 and United Communication Industry retreated eight to 248.
Brokers said the index was expected to move sideways on Wednesday as investors would closely follow the debate.
Support is seen around 1,030 points and resistance around 1,065 on Wednesday, brokers said.
